actionResult.summary: Review 013 Apply: implementation materially satisfies A1 readiness/Owner-authorized Full Test/no-Run/result-authority contract, package payload hashes pass, mutation surface stays within approved flowkitMutationScope, typecheck/build/lint/OpenSpec strict and 108 focused tests pass, and formal `flowkit verify` reproduces the exact published verification fingerprint/selection. One author blocker remains: non-Windows timeout is classified as re-entry-safe `timed-out-cancelled` after SIGKILL of only the direct child, while the approved A1 spec permits re-entry only after the prior child/process tree is proven terminal. A disposable Linux proof observed `timed-out-cancelled` while a spawned descendant survived and continued mutation, so bounded at-least-once re-entry is not physically closed across supported platforms.

reviewFindings.title: Non-Windows timeout is marked re-entry-safe without proving descendant process-tree termination
reviewFindings.problem: The approved A1 core-model spec requires that a fresh Full Test attempt MAY re-enter from `authorized` only when the prior child/process tree has been proven terminal. 013 implements owned whole-tree cancellation for Windows, but the unchanged non-Windows `runCommand()` timeout path sends SIGKILL only to the direct child PID and then returns `timed-out-cancelled` when that launcher closes. `runDeliveryFullTest()` treats `timed-out-cancelled` as a safe terminal transport failure, leaves raw status `authorized`, writes no executionBlock, and therefore permits an explicit later attempt. This proves only launcher termination, not descendant process-tree termination.
reviewFindings.contractRef: openspec/changes/delivery-readiness-and-full-test-behavior/specs/flowkit-core-model/spec.md — `authorized crash 可 bounded re-entry`: only when prior child/process tree is proven terminal; transport-failure scenario: only process-proven-terminal failure MAY remain authorized for re-entry
reviewFindings.invariant: Without a running/attempt ledger, every timeout path that leaves Full Test re-enterable at raw `authorized` must prove the entire owned prior process tree terminal. If whole-tree termination is not proven, Policy must fail closed and prohibit overlap rather than label the attempt safely cancelled.
evidence: 013 `src/services/delivery-full-test-service.ts` treats outcome.kind=`timed-out-cancelled` as execution-error with no executionBlock; raw status remains authorized and can later re-enter.

Exact current `src/shared/external-command.ts` non-win32 timeout path calls only `child.kill('SIGKILL')`; once the direct child closes it returns `kind=timed-out-cancelled`. No POSIX process-group/tree cancellation or descendant termination proof exists.

Disposable Linux physical proof: a parent Node process spawned a descendant that wrote a marker after 500ms; `runCommand(..., timeout=100, platform=linux)` returned `{kind:"timed-out-cancelled"}`, yet the descendant later wrote `descendant-survived`, proving the old process tree was still executing after Flowkit had classified the timeout as safe terminal cancellation.

The current 03 Full Test route is itself multi-process (`npm -> verification.ts -> Node/OpenSpec/npm children`), so this is applicable to the actual A1 execution shape, not merely a synthetic single-process edge case.
013 Windows tests correctly prove whole-tree taskkill semantics; there is no equivalent non-Windows descendant-survival regression.
reviewFindings.impact: After a Linux/macOS timeout, Flowkit can return control with raw status still `authorized` while descendants from the old Full Test continue running. A later explicit Full Test can then overlap with the stale tree, invalidating the approved bounded at-least-once/re-entry invariant and allowing concurrent generated-file/process mutation despite the lifecycle claiming the prior attempt was safely cancelled.
reviewFindings.location: src/shared/external-command.ts non-win32 timeout branch; src/services/delivery-full-test-service.ts timed-out-cancelled classification; tests/unit/services/delivery-full-test-service.test.ts timeout coverage
reviewFindings.requiredOutcome: Close non-Windows timeout ownership to the same invariant as Windows: either prove the owned descendant process tree terminal before returning a re-entry-safe cancellation outcome, or conservatively classify unproven termination as outcome-unknown and persist/block through the existing A1 executionBlock semantics. Keep the solution bounded; do not add a scheduler, running state, attempt ledger or background supervisor.
acceptance: A real non-Windows descendant-survival fixture cannot produce re-entry-safe `timed-out-cancelled` while any descendant remains alive.
Every timeout that leaves raw Full Test status `authorized` and permits later re-entry has a demonstrated whole-process-tree terminal proof.

If non-Windows whole-tree termination cannot be proven, the attempt becomes fail-closed/non-reenterable through the existing outcome-unknown/executionBlock boundary rather than fabricated Verification failed.
Windows taskkill whole-tree semantics remain green and unchanged in authority.
Formal Change Verification selects and physically executes the new/updated timeout regression and remains passed on the revised exact candidate.
